To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
macrolide efflux in S. pneumonia is mediated by a dual efflux pump (Mef and Mel) that is induced by macrolides.

(i) the macrolide resistance phenotype of S. pneumoniae is mediated by the efflux of macrolides by a proton motive force-dependent efflux pump, Mef, and an ATP-binding cassette transporter, Mel, and that both genes are required for full resistance; (ii) the expression of both genes is inducible in the presence of erythromycin; and (iii) mefE is more important than mel for the resistance phenotype.
the macrolide efflux pump Mef and the closely related pump Mel are both required for macrolides resistance in S. pneumonae and that both genes are erythromycin inducible.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel efflux pump inhibitors that can be used to treat macrolide-resistant S. pneumoniae infections.
the mechanism of macrolide resistance mediated by efflux in S. pneumonia.
the development of a novel macrolide resistance mechanism in S. pneumonia, mediated by the mega and related elements, that has emerged worldwide as a clinically important problem.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
both mef and mel are required for the novel efflux pump in S. pneumonia.
macrolide resistance mediated by the mega and related elements in S. pneumonia is a dual-efflux pump system, and both Mef and the related protein Mel are essential components of this efflux system.
macrolide efflux in S. pneumonia requires the expression of both the Mef and Mel proteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the macrolide resistance efflux system in S. pnuemoniae is a two component system, with the mef component being responsible for the proton motive force component and the mel component responsible for ATP binding.
the efflux pump Mef-Mel is inducible and that both genes are required for efflux.
the mefE-mel operon is required for macromolecular resistance in Streptociocus pneumoniae and other Gram positive bacteria and that the operon is inducible.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the efflux pump in S. pneumonia is inducible.
the mel gene is also required for the efflux-mediated macroid resistance system in pneumococcus and that the system appears to be inducible by the presence of macrolide antibiotics.
macrolide resistance is mediated by two genes, Mef and Mel, which are transcribed as a polycistronic operon and are inducible by the macrolide.
